conservation.condition_narrative: There has been no conservation of the painting since arriving at SCMA. A “greasy substance” suspected to be from a visitor was removed in-house in 2014.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Smith College Museum of Art in 2025.
conservation.technical_description: Metal frame sewed into the sides of the painting.

remarks_1999: Stretcher inscriptions indicate preparation of support. "My first painting [fall 1948] — a dead tree surrounded by the autumn is very gentle and pleasant and high in key but it holds its place on the wall alone more than forty feet away" (O'Keeffe to Vernon Hunter, 30 October 1948, YCAL). Titled *Grey Trees – Fall of 48* by O'Keeffe on Abiquiú Notebooks photograph. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A bare, gray tree stands on a stretch of red earth, its outer limbs soft and smoke-like. Bright yellow and orange foliage from other trees fills the space behind the gray tree. A small green bush grows at the tree's base.
imageCaption: Courtesy of Smith College Museum of Art.
